title: Keeping the Notes Beside the Image
transcript:
A regional archive is digitising thousands of photographs donated by local families. The project originally aimed to make high-quality images available online as quickly as possible. After a trial release, however, archivists discovered that the information surrounding a photograph could be as valuable as the photograph itself.

Some donors had written names on the backs of prints. Others had added uncertain guesses on separate sheets or explained a scene during a recorded conversation. In the first version of the catalogue, these different sources were combined into a single description. Readers could not tell which names had been written at the time and which had been suggested decades later.

The problem became clear when two families identified the same person differently. Rather than choosing the more confident donor's account, the archive preserved both claims and recorded their sources. A later contribution, showing the same group from another angle, helped resolve the disagreement. Without the earlier notes, researchers would not have known why the original description was uncertain.

The revised catalogue now separates visible information, donor comments and the archive's own conclusions. Users can search the plain-language description, then open a record of how it was assembled. This adds work for staff, and the project is releasing fewer images each week than first planned.

The director argues that the slower pace is justified. A digital collection should not turn a provisional identification into an apparently unquestionable fact merely because it appears in a neat search result. The archive is still improving access, but it is also preserving the path by which knowledge was produced. That history may allow future researchers to correct a mistake rather than unknowingly repeat it.

questions.prompt: What weakness was found in the first online catalogue?
options: The photographs could be viewed only by their donors.
It combined information from different sources without showing their origins.
It included only photographs taken in the same year.
It refused to display any names written on original prints.
questions.answer: It combined information from different sources without showing their origins.
questions.explanation: 最初把当时的题注、后来的猜测等合并，读者看不出信息来源和时间。

questions.prompt: How did the archive initially handle the conflicting identifications?
options: It deleted the photograph from the collection.
It accepted whichever family had donated more material.
It preserved both claims and recorded their sources.
It removed every personal name from the website.
questions.answer: It preserved both claims and recorded their sources.
questions.explanation: 档案馆保留两种说法及各自来源，而非选择更自信的一方。

questions.prompt: What consequence followed the revised cataloguing approach?
options: Fewer images could be released each week.
Staff no longer needed to check donor comments.
Users lost the ability to search descriptions.
All uncertain information was permanently discarded.
questions.answer: Fewer images could be released each week.
questions.explanation: 分开记录信息及形成过程增加了工作量，每周发布的图像数量因此减少。

questions.prompt: Why does the director consider the extra work worthwhile?
options: Digital images automatically become historically accurate.
A confident description is always more useful than a qualified one.
The archive can now avoid accepting corrections.
It preserves uncertainty and evidence that may support future corrections.
questions.answer: It preserves uncertainty and evidence that may support future corrections.
questions.explanation: 保留信息形成路径与不确定性，可使后来的研究者纠错而非重复错误。
